newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian share market closes steady, outlook flat.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian share market closes steady, outlook flat.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange closed little changed on Monday in the lack of any fresh impetus on the domestic market and sideways trend on major European bourses, traders said.
The BUX index closed at a preliminary 5,929.87 points, down 14.59.

Traders said foreign investors were less active than before. "Foreigners were not very active and the very strong pressure from local investors has also eased," Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings. "Turnover isn't very high in west Europe either."
Analysts said the market's near-term outlook is mixed as a result of different impacts.
"The market is currently fairly flat, I guess it's torn between conflicting influences," said Stephen O'Sullivan, analyst at MC-BBL Securities in London.

"The things which are keeping the market strong in Hungary are MOL and Richter which have performed very very well but how much influence they have beyond the short-term, is difficult to say at the moment."
On Monday practically only oil company MOL, chemicals TVK and machinery Mezogep had significant volumes, another trader said.

"MOL's lower volume is certainly in link with the start of subscriptions," the trader said. "Domestic investors now contemplate how many shares they will be allocated and will decide about purchases on the bourse accordingly."
More than 700,000 MOL stocks changed hands -- less than in the past few days --, bolstered by an agency cross for 405,000 shares. MOL closed unchanged at 3,475 forints.
Subscriptions for MOL's domestic offer began today.
TVK dipped 10 forints to end at 2,840, while Mezogep put on 40 forints to end at 2,490.
Elsewhere, drugs maker Human edged up 10 forints to 2,730 despite it reported a fall in operating profit and just a shade higher after-tax profit in the first three months.
Some of the market's leading issues, including drugs maker Egis, hotelier Danubius, MOL and OTP Bank have not yet published their earnings report and market participants expect some effect from them.

"My impression is that people think MOL's earnings is going to be quite reasonable," MC-BBL's O'Sullivan said. "This year is likely to be quite a good year for MOL and I suspect that the quarterly figures will reflect that."

Two new stocks began to trade on Monday. Currency futures trading firm Masodik Deviza Factory closed at 13,300 forints, while venture capital company Riziko Factory at 9,150 forints. Both were issued at 10,000 forints.
